question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The implementation path exists internally, but promoting it to plugin runtime changes both the public plugin contract and the Discord bot-credential mutation boundary.

options.title: Design a gated runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit authorization, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

options.title: Keep presence as action/config only
options.body: Keep dynamic presence limited to static config, auto-presence, and the existing default-off `setPresence` message action.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this issue behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a presence-only runtime API.

recommendation.title: Design a gated runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit authorization, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily whether to add a public plugin-runtime seam that reintroduces a Discord-specific runtime slot.
